title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript note on the divided-power de Rham complex. It is a typed page, p. 140, from Exposé IX of SGA 7 I (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', §11, the semistable case: orthogonality theorem and description of the component group). It was probably reused as scrap paper and ended up in cote 136; the neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on comparing simplicial/de Rham cochains.

Setting: S is a strictly henselian trait with fraction field K. A_K is an abelian variety with semistable reduction. A is its Néron model, A^o the identity component, and Φ_o = A_o/A_o^o the group of components of the special fibre. For n = ℓ^{r+1}, the finite part (_nA)^f is the r-th component of the Barsotti–Tate pro-group T_ℓ(A_K)^f. The group scheme _nΨ (defined in 11.6.6, presumably as a quotient of finite flat parts of n-torsion) has generic fibre identified, via the first relation of (5.5.8), with the constant group M_n = M ⊗ Z/nZ. Here M is the lattice attached to the toric part (character / monodromy lattice).

Lemma 11.6.8: _nΨ is étale over S, and the generic isomorphism extends uniquely to an open immersion _nΨ → M_n.

Proof as given:
- Étaleness need only be checked on the special fibre. That fibre is _nA_o/_nA_o^o ⊂ Φ_o, which is étale. Flatness is implicit from the construction in 11.6.6.
- Hence _nΨ is normal, since it is étale over a regular base.
- M_n is finite over S, so the morphism on the generic fibre extends by normality (integral-closure argument).
- The kernel is an étale separated group with trivial generic fibre, so it is trivial (3.1.3).
- An étale monomorphism is an open immersion (EGA IV 17.9.1).

The page then defines _nΦ = (_nA)^f/(_nA^o)^f ⊂ _nΨ, a finite open subscheme. This leads to the description of Φ in terms of M and the monodromy pairing.
errors: The typescript sentence 'et comme _nΨ donc ce noyau est séparé' is missing a predicate. It should read roughly 'et comme _nΨ est séparé, ce noyau est séparé'. This is a typing slip, not a mathematical error.
Flatness of _nΨ, needed for étaleness, is not re-argued here. It presumably follows from the construction in 11.6.6. This is a minor gap only on this page in isolation.

ideas.what: Étaleness of _nΨ and its open immersion into the constant group M ⊗ Z/n, extending the generic isomorphism coming from the Barsotti–Tate / monodromy relations (5.5.8)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's description of the Néron component group via the monodromy pairing (semistable case)

ideas.what: An étale monomorphism is an open immersion; extending morphisms from a normal scheme into a finite scheme over a normal base
ideas.modern_name: EGA IV 17.9.1; extension via integral closure

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript leaf of the published SGA 7 I Exposé IX (p. 140, Lemma 11.6.8), apparently reused as scrap paper within the 1976 de Rham notes. Its content is published and well known. The only curiosity is archival: a published typescript page physically sits in this cote.
transcription_corrections: The page belongs to SGA 7 I Exposé IX (page header '- 140 -  IX'), not to the de Rham notes. The '458' and '70' are archive numberings.
'et comme _nΨ donc ce noyau est séparé': the original typescript omits 'est séparé' after _nΨ. The transcription faithfully reproduces this slip.
In 'nAo/nAoo ⊂ Ao/Aoo = Φo', the superscript 'o' denotes the identity component: _nA_o/_nA_o^o ⊂ A_o/A_o^o = Φ_o.
